### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getLocales (literal, a string literal in negotiatedReaderLocale))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`  _(via getLocales (literal, a string literal in negotiatedReaderLocale))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e2ead3c187db5e17d481065094afc5a72e15803` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `08eb607940dc472312e7805e6f243c652c45331a` — the merge of head `6724fe5d6859f1478430b99a1f3142b2468495f3` into base `0e2ead3c187db5e17d481065094afc5a72e15803`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 08eb607940dc472312e7805e6f243c652c45331a && git checkout 08eb607940dc472312e7805e6f243c652c45331a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0e2ead3c187db5e17d481065094afc5a72e15803 6724fe5d6859f1478430b99a1f3142b2468495f3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0e2ead3c187db5e17d481065094afc5a72e15803 && git merge --no-ff 6724fe5d6859f1478430b99a1f3142b2468495f3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e2ead3c187db5e17d481065094afc5a72e15803
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0e2ead3c187db5e17d481065094afc5a72e15803` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `589d440206c6089d1fdd9d6a3045def5a576cede`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/lifecycle-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/reader-locale-labels.ts

Inputs read: card #34454 body and all 6 comments; PR #34496 body, 8-file list, both PR comments; the net diff against merge-base e8cba8fe; the check-runs on this head. The remaining 4 files (two plugin-approvals test files, `operation-message.test.ts`, the changeset) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `renderOperationMessage` (published, `@objectstack/spec/system`): the override lookup changes from `translate(key, locale, params)` to `translate(key, locale)`, and the answer is interpolated once by `interpolateValidationMessage`. Right. It is the call the function's own docblock already states at step 1 of its resolution order, and both in-repo `II18nService` implementations return the raw template when no params are handed (`FileI18nAdapter.t`, `packages/services/service-i18n/src/file-i18n-adapter.ts`; the memory fallback, `packages/core/src/fallbacks/memory-i18n.ts`). Their placeholder rule is the renderer's: the same `{{word}}` pattern, an absent or null value left verbatim. So for every override served by an in-repo service the output is unchanged, except the one case the change targets: a parameter VALUE that itself holds a placeholder is now printed as written.
- Accept-set of `renderOperationMessage`: unchanged. Signature, `RenderOperationMessageInput`, `RenderOperationMessageOptions` and `ValidationMessageTranslator` (params still optional) are untouched; no key added or removed; no generated artifact implied.
- Other consumers of the changed path (objectql delete-cascade and duplicate-record, plugin-security, plugin-sharing, plugin-audit, service-storage, rest, runtime): they hand an `i18n.t` wrapper, so they inherit the single-pass behaviour with the same output for well-formed overrides. Right.
- `negotiatedReaderLocale` (plugin-approvals, module-internal export, not in the package's published surface by this diff): the former private `negotiatedLocale`, widened to accept an absent service and an absent request, both passing through. Right; body matches objectql's `negotiatedMessageLocale` line for line (same pass-through cases, same `resolveBundleLocale` over the offered key set).
- Both refusals now ask the override with the negotiated tag. Wire code, status and the `CODE: message` envelope are untouched by the diff. Right.
- BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES docblock: comment-only repair (card nit N1). Right.
- Gate verdicts on this head: no check-run concluded failure. Concluded success include Build Core, Type Check source gates, consumer gates and debt ledger, every Lint job, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Test Core 4/8, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI. PENDING at the time of reading, so not verdicts: Test Core 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 of 8, Type Check workspace, Type Check UI, Test UI 1 to 16 of 16. This record does not stand in for them.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` patch and `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` patch match what the diff publishes: a defect fix toward the documented call, no accept-set change, no new export from either package's public entry. The changeset states the behaviour change in its own words (the template is asked without the parameters and filled once) and the one visible difference.

Clause-②: no — holds. No declared capability is narrowed: the docblock contract was already `translate('errors.KEY', locale)`, and the translator type still admits the three-argument form. Residual, stated for the record: a third-party `II18nService` that does something with `params` beyond `{{name}}` substitution (count-based plural selection, another placeholder syntax) no longer receives them on the operation-override path. No in-repo service does either, and the catalog's Interpolation section already names `{{name}}` as the convention, so this stays inside patch.

Metadata-protocol: none — holds; no schema, no authorable key.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: "Needs a contract review (packages/spec/src path limb) at head 589d440206". Answered by this record.
- Dev deviation, pins in the two existing harness files instead of new per-card files (ruling record 6583487846): test placement, lane seat's ACCEPT; no contract effect.
- Dev deviation, patch for both packages: answered in ②, correct.
- Dev `out_of_scope_findings`, `renderValidationMessage` keeps ask-with-params-then-interpolate because "its params are a field label, API name and authored constraint values, not row content": the reason given does NOT hold as written. Read on `main`, the sibling catalog's templates carry `{{value}}`, which is the offending value the user typed or imported (`option_unavailable`, `invalid_initial_state`, every `import_*` key). On the override path a cell value such as `{{label}}` is therefore expanded by the second pass, the same defect this PR removes one catalog over. Leaving it out of this PR is right (the file is outside the claimed file surface and outside this diff), but "noted, not filed" is not: ESCALATED to the lane seat as a follow-up card for `packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts`, same one-line fix and one pin. Effect is display-only (the expansion can only yield the message's own label, field name or constraint values), so it does not block this head.
- File surface: the diff stays inside the amended claim (comment 6931164180). No breach.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to find.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts` (hits), against the card, record 6927238180's nits and its first consumers:

- The one-line body change makes the code agree with three sentences of the file's own contract that it previously contradicted or strained: step 1 of the resolution order, the Interpolation section ("an unknown placeholder is left verbatim"), and "the label and the title are its parameters" for row content. Tried to break it: an empty params object, a missing param, a null param, a key miss (key echoed back), a throwing translator, and a translator that ignores params all produce the same text as before; only a value holding a `{{name}}` whose name is another param of the same message differs, and that difference is the fix. The docblock claim "Resolution order (identical to renderValidationMessage)" still holds for the order.
- The comment added at the call site is accurate against both in-repo services.
- The docblock repair restores the paragraph break and changes no meaning.

Implementing files, sentence by sentence:

- `reader-locale-labels.ts`: the docblock's pass-through list (no service, no `getLocales`, a throwing or empty answer, no match, absent request stays absent) is exactly the body. "Every lookup this plugin asks the i18n service ... asks it with this tag" was checked against every `t(` and `renderOperationMessage(` site in `plugin-approvals/src` at head: `readerLabelsFor`, `refusalLocalization` and `userFacingRefusal` are the only three, and all three negotiate. Holds.
- `lifecycle-hooks.ts`: `refusalLocalization` returns the negotiated tag; its single caller passes it to `readerLabelsFor`, which negotiates again, idempotent because an offered tag matches itself exactly. Label and override are now asked with one tag, as the docblock says. A missing or throwing service still degrades the wording and never the lock.
- `approval-service.ts`: `userFacingRefusal` negotiates against `i18nServiceSource`; `approvals-plugin.ts` wires that and `messageTranslator` from the same `i18nService()` provider, so the comment "the same service the translator reads" is true as wired. A host that supplies only `messageTranslator` gets the raw tag, the prior behaviour, which the comment states.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — `lifecycle-hooks.ts`, "The built-in catalog matches the negotiated tag as it matched the raw one": true for the four built-in locales today (en, zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES), because negotiation stays inside one language. It would stop being true for a zh-TW writer if the built-in catalog ever gained a Traditional table while the service held only zh-CN. objectql's `negotiatedMessageLocale` has the same property, and the card asks for exactly that behaviour. Accepted deviation; no change on this head.
- N2 (nit) — `operation-message.ts`, `RenderOperationMessageOptions.translate` is still described only as "an II18nService.t-compatible lookup"; it does not say the lookup is asked for the template with no params. The function docblock and the call-site comment do say it. Fold into the follow-up card named in ③, or leave.

### ① Derived judgments

- The delta is one file. `git diff 589d4402 6724fe5d --stat` lists `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-permission-refusal-override.test.ts` alone, 6 insertions and 1 deletion, over two commits (3279a191, 6724fe5d). Neither file is in this PR's diff. Before this PR the renderer called the wrapper with an empty params object; now it calls it with key and locale, and the wrapper forwards the missing third argument as `undefined`. That is the whole change this consumer sees.
- User-visible output of this consumer: unchanged. `permission_denied` is rendered with no params, and its four built-in sentences carry no placeholder. An override sentence is returned by `t` as written and interpolated once against an empty set, which leaves any placeholder verbatim, as the service's own pass over an empty object did. Status 403, code `PERMISSION_DENIED`, and the fall back to the built-in sentence on a missing, unresolvable or throwing service are the same code path as before. The previous record's claim, "they inherit the single-pass behaviour with the same output for well-formed overrides", holds for this consumer.

The test keeps `expect(a.body?.error?.message).toBe(OVERRIDE_ZH)` on all three refusals (app, dashboard, list view), keeps the CONTROL case and both failure cases untouched, and replaces `expect.anything()` for the third argument with exactly `undefined`. The old matcher accepted any non-null value; the new one accepts one value, so it is the stricter assertion, and it now pins the contract this PR states (the template is asked by key and locale, no params) at a second door. The old assertion could not pass on the previous head: `expect.anything()` rejects `undefined`. The edit moves the pin to the new call shape; it does not remove a behaviour pin to get green.
- `import '@objectstack/metadata'` at module top: a side-effect import in a test file, no assertion touched. It loads at collection what `HttpDispatcher` reaches by dynamic import. No contract effect.

The file is outside the amended claim's file surface (comment 6931164180 names plugin-approvals, the spec file and its test, and the changeset). - The follow-up escalated by the previous record's ③ (`renderValidationMessage` keeps ask-with-params-then-interpolate) is not touched by the delta and stays escalated to the lane seat.

### ④ Design judgment

Short, because nothing in Scope moved: `operation-message.ts` and the three plugin-approvals files are byte-identical to the head the previous record read sentence by sentence, and that reading stands.

What the delta adds to the design reading of `renderOperationMessage`: a second door, in another package, now states the same sentence as the function's docblock and the call-site comment ("asked by key and locale, no params: the renderer interpolates it once"). What it did not state is that a consumer's translator can observe the call shape itself, and that an in-repo pin in `packages/runtime` asserted the third argument, so that pin could not pass on the head it passed (the rework report names CI red at 589d440206). - Changeset: root `.changeset/34454-…md`, patch for `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` and `@objectstack/spec` (both published). I checked each sentence against the diff:
  - "both now negotiate the tag against the locales the service holds first": yes, `refusalLocalization` and `userFacingRefusal` both call `negotiatedReaderLocale`.
  - "the object label … was already asked this way": yes, `readerLabelsFor` already negotiated.

**Delta `589d4402` → `6724fe5d` (test-only, one file)**

Since `renderOperationMessage` now asks for the template by key and locale only, the pin now asserts that shape (`…, 'zh-CN', undefined`). It still asserts the 403, `PERMISSION_DENIED` and the override text, so the override path stays pinned end to end at the `/meta` door.
- It adds an `import '@objectstack/metadata'` so the dynamic import's cost is paid when the file is collected rather than inside a timed case. This is test timing only, with no production change.
- This corrects one point of my first read: I had checked only that no PRODUCTION caller relied on `translate` receiving `params`, which holds. One TEST pinned the argument, CI caught it, and this delta fixes it in the right place, the stale pin, not the renderer.

**Spot checks (mine)**
